title.narrative: UNDP COSED: Social Cohesion, Security and Rule of Law
UNDP COSED: Social Cohesion, Security and Rule of Law

description.narrative:
Project name: UNDP COSED: Social Cohesion, Security and Rule of Law
Agreement partner and implementer: UNDP
Implementation period: 1 June 2020- 30 June 2021
Amount of financial support by Sida: 50 000 000 SEK
Background: The judiciary sector in Burkina Faso is plagued by chronic inefficiency, high levels of corruption, recurrent strikes and high levels of inaccessibility. Furthermore, Burkina Faso has experienced a dramatic deterioration of the security situation during the last few years, with wide ramifications on societal functioning. The consequences of the security context, with its numerous attacks on civilians and armed forces, include an extremely rapidly escalating displacement crisis. The deteriorating security has an impact on social cohesion, as the attacks have had both ethnic and religious connotations, connotations which have been instrumentalised by different factions.
The weaknesses of the judiciary sector combined with the security context have wide repercussions on the respect of human rights in Burkina Faso. In order to respond to the challenges described above UNDP (United Nations Development Programme) has designed a programme with three components focusing on rule of law, the security sector and on activities aiming to strengthen social cohesion. Sweden would focus its support to the first two components.
The programme is in line with the first pillar of the Prevention and Peacebuilding Assessment (PPBA) on Security and Rule of Law. The PPBA was undertaken jointly in 2019 by the World Bank, the UN and the EU. The programme is also in line with Burkina Faso's National Plan for Economic and Social Development (PNDES). The total budget of the programme is approximately 16 million USD for a programme period of 2,5 years (2019-2021). Sweden's contribution would be 50 million SEK for an activity period of 12 months.
The intended impact of the programme is the following: "Improve the effectiveness of institutions by 2021, so that the populations of Burkina Faso, especially those most exposed to the risks of conflict and insecurity, live in peace and security under the rule of law. It aims to make burkinabè communities, particularly women, the actors and beneficiaries of human rights, justice, security, accountability and social cohesion."
The programme has three components and each of those have a certain number of expected results:
1) Justice and human rights - The capacity of the justice system to fight impunity is strengthened - The population has better access to justice - Human rights are better respected and monitoring and reporting of human rights violations is better ensured.
2) Security - National stakeholders are capable of implementing and ensuring the monitoring and evaluation of security policies and strategies - Security forces, while respecting human rights, is more effective in carrying out its missions - Confidence between the population and the security forces has improved.
3) Social cohesion - Mining companies respect the provisions of the mining code relating to their responsibilities in terms of social and environmental issues, and repair of environmental damage caused by mining is more efficient - Farmers and herders respect the routes of the transhumance tracks - Traditional and modern mechanisms for conflict prevention and management are more operational, inclusive and work in synergy in the form of an integrated infrastructure for peace - The population adopt a tolerant religious practice - Public institutions (the National Parliament and the Higher State Control and Anti-Corruption Authority) and civil society are able to contribute to social cohesion through the control of accountability.

Projektnamn: UNDP COSED: Social Cohesion, Security and Rule of Law Avtalspartner och genomförande: UNDP
Implementeringsperiod: 1 juni 2020- 30 juni 2021
Finansiellt stöd från Sida: 50 000 000 SEK
Bakgrund: Rättsväsendet i Burkina Faso plågas av kronisk ineffektivitet, höga nivåer av korruption, återkommande strejker och höga nivåer av otillgänglighet. Dessutom har Burkina Faso upplevt en dramatisk försämring av säkerhetssituationen under de senaste åren, med stora konsekvenser för samhällsfunktionen. Konsekvenserna av säkerhetskontexten, med dess många attacker mot civila och väpnade styrkor, inkluderar en snabbt ökande flyktingkris. Den försämrade säkerheten påverkar den sociala sammanhållningen, eftersom attackerna har haft både etniska och religiösa konnotationer, konnotationer som har instrumentaliserats av olika fraktioner.
Rättssektorns svagheter i kombination med säkerhetsförhållandena har stora återverkningar på respekten för de mänskliga rättigheterna i Burkina Faso. För att svara på de utmaningar som beskrivs ovan har UNDP (FN: s utvecklingsprogram) utformat ett program med tre komponenter som fokuserar på att stärka rättsstatens principer, säkerhetssektorn och på aktiviteter som syftar till att stärka den sociala sammanhållningen. Sverige fokuserar sitt stöd till de två första komponenterna.
Programmet är i linje med den första pelaren i förebyggande och fredsbyggande bedömningen (PPBA) om säkerhet och rättsstat. PPBA genomfördes gemensamt 2019 av Världsbanken, FN och EU. Programmet är också i linje med Burkina Fasos nationella plan för ekonomisk och social utveckling (PNDES).
Programmets totala budget är cirka 16 miljoner USD för en programperiod på 2,5 år (2019-2021). Sveriges bidrag är 50 miljoner SEK för en aktivitetsperiod på 12 månader.
Programmets avsedda övergripande mål är följande: "Förbättra institutionernas effektivitet fram till 2021, så att befolkningen i Burkina Faso, särskilt de som är mest utsatta för riskerna för konflikter och osäkerhet, lever i fred och säkerhet under rättsstatens principer. Det syftar till att göra burkinier, särskilt kvinnor, till aktörerna och förmånstagarna av mänskliga rättigheter, rättvisa, säkerhet, ansvar och social sammanhållning. "
Programmet har tre komponenter och var och en av dem har ett visst antal förväntade resultat:
1) Rättssektorn och mänskliga rättigheter - Rättssystemets förmåga att bekämpa straffrihet stärks - Befolkningen har bättre tillgång till rättvisa - Mänskliga rättigheter respekteras mer och övervakning och rapportering av kränkningar av mänskliga rättigheter stärks.
2) Säkerhetsektorn - Nationella intressenter kan genomföra och säkerställa övervakning och utvärdering av säkerhetspolicyer och strategier - Säkerhetsstyrkorna, medan de respekterar mänskliga rättigheter, är mer effektiva i att utföra sina uppdrag - Förtroendet mellan befolkningen och säkerhetsstyrkorna har förbättrats.
3) Social sammanhållning - Gruvföretag respekterar bestämmelserna i lagstiftningen när det gäller deras ansvar i fråga om sociala och miljömässiga frågor, och ersättning av miljöskador orsakade av gruvdrift är effektivare - Jordbrukare och boskapsskötare respekterar vandringsvägarna - Traditionella och moderna mekanismer för förebyggande och hantering av konflikter är mer operativa, inkluderande och fungerar i synergi som en integrerad infrastruktur för fred - Befolkningen antar en tolerant religiös praxis - Offentliga institutioner (nationella parlamentet och myndigheten för högre kontroll och antikorruption) och det civila samhället kan bidra till social sammanhållning genom ansvarsutkrävande

The intended impact of the programme is the following: "Improve the effectiveness of institutions by 2021, so that the populations of Burkina Faso, especially those most exposed to the risks of conflict and insecurity, live in peace and security under the rule of law. It aims to make burkinabè communities, particularly women, the actors and beneficiaries of human rights, justice, security, accountability and social cohesion." The programme has three components and each of those have a certain number of expected results: 1) Justice and human rights - The capacity of the justice system to fight impunity is strengthened - The population has better access to justice - Human rights are better respected and monitoring and reporting of human rights violations is better ensured. 2) Security - National stakeholders are capable of implementing and ensuring the monitoring and evaluation of security policies and strategies - The FDS, while respecting human rights, is more effective in carrying out its missions - Confidence between the population and the security forces has improved. 3) Social cohesion - Mining companies respect the provisions of the mining code relating to their responsibilities in terms of social and environmental issues, and repair of environmental damage caused by mining is more efficient - Farmers and herders respect the routes of the transhumance tracks - Traditional and modern mechanisms for conflict prevention and management are more operational, inclusive and work in synergy in the form of an integrated infrastructure for peace - The population adopt a tolerant religious practice - Public institutions (the National Parliament and the Higher State Control and Anti-Corruption Authority) and civil society are able to contribute to social cohesion through the control of accountability.

The contribution covered three impact areas a) justice and human rights b) security and c) social cohesion. These impact areas were broken down to 16 different results areas comprising altogether 166 planned activities. With regard to justice and human rights, the support was mainly technical in nature. The results include the development of manuals regarding court procedures and management framework for the different roles and responsibilities of different actors in the court. This included developing legal criteria for establishing a legal claim in addition to the procedures for how it can be brought to court. The legal term that is referred to here is the minimum standards of evidence (technically known as a threshold reference), in French un référentiel des seuils. In addition, the program managed to set up seven legal clinics that offered free or low cost legal advice that were run by local civil society organisations. More than 15, 000 people have been participating in awareness raising sessions according to the annual narrative report covering 2023. According to the same report, 81 cases of legal aid have been granted to vulnerable persons in 2023. In other cases, UNDP has organized criminal hearings and updated the websites of the Ministry of Justice. Other results include the organisation of and cleanup of an evidence room. The reporting claims that these result examples contributed to reducing the backlog of legal cases and improved the conditions for access to justice. With regard to the second impact area, security, the COSED program created a variety of results entailing a combination of the construction of infrastructure, producing and delivering trainings, handbooks and advising services. Reportedly, the building of infrastructure has been financed by Germany according to the updated prodoc from 2021. This entails the construction lecture halls for security personnel, barracks for security personnel and offices for police and gendarmerie which falls outside Official Development Assistance (ODA) eligible support. However, the material support that was granted in terms of equipping the Interministerial Committee for National Security with computer and software can be considered as ODA eligible because it supports capacity building of security and justice systems required for the prevention of violent extremism. Trainings were conducted in Human Rights, community policing and gender sensitive policing and handbooks were created in these mentioned domains as well. With regard to advising, the program worked in advising on how the plan for Security Sector Reform could be implemented, in addition to reviewing law texts governing the setup of a national security architecture. As mentioned, the program worked with the Interministerial Committee for National Security which has a key role in coordinating Burkinabe security agencies in a workshop between august 7-12, 2023 in a security threat assessment and prioritization. This can be considered as ODA eligible as these activities are part of an overall Security Sector Reform process.
Results pertaining to the third impact area on social cohesion was mainly around awareness raising and training of civil society leaders on how mining companies can be monitored. In addition, the program cooperated with relevant authorities in creating a strategy for national reconciliation and social cohesion. The program also worked engaged in promoting a dialogue between religious leaders in the country. The program also contributed to, according to the midterm evaluation, strengthening the national system of monitoring religious discourse through the oversight of ONOFAR (National Observatory of Religious Events) with regard to preaches in the religious media. (p. 50) This organisation analysed 500 religious speeches in order to gain more information on the topic of possible religious intolerance. Reportedly, the large majority of speeches were not labelled intolerant.
The program also supported the National Observatory of the Prevention and Management of Community Conflict. For example, the annual report for 2023 reported that 1, 057 members of this Observatory were trained. Only 95 of the participants were women.
With regard to the topic of National Reconciliation, the program supported the elaboration of a national strategy for reconciliation. A National Reconciliation Strategy 20222026 by Ministry of Solidarity, Humanitarian Action was adopted by the Burkinabe government. However, this document is more of a funding proposal for what can be done in the area of national reconciliation, if the funds are provided for. In addition, this Strategy seemingly competes with the responsibilities of a State Minister that was appointed by the Junta in 2022 in charge of Social Cohesion and National Reconciliation. Therefore, the responsibilities of National Reconciliation was to a certain extent duplicated into two offices, one within the government and the other within the presidential administration. This suggests that the important topic of national reconciliation was not coordinated and lacked focus.
Assessment of achieved results in relation to the objectives
In December 2023, the Swedish government decided to phase out the Strategy with Burkina Faso. Originally, the activity period would in December 2023, but after the phasing out decision, the Embassy and the UNDP agreed to extend the activity period until September 2024. Sida assesses that the phase out decision did not in a fundamental way change the implementation of the activities. UNDP Burkina Faso has carried out a wide range of activities. Assessing the impact and usefulness of these activities is challenging for several reasons. Firstly, the reporting that account for different activities are generally not phrased in an analytical context that enables an understanding of how and why the different activities have an impact vis à vis the Burkinabe institutions. The Burkinabe institutions, which ultimately are the real beneficiaries of this program are pretty much in the background in the reporting. This makes it challenging to understand the significance of the different outputs. For example, the evaluation report mentions the career management of magistrates as part of the achievements (p. 30). From Sida's perspective it unclear why this is important and prioritized and how this contributes the goal. Secondly, the scope of activities are wide and encompass three result areas with 16 output areas and 166 activities all planned to be carried out within two and a half years. This suggests that there is a lack of prioritization that is based on an understanding where the real bottlenecks lie. Furthermore, the COSED program is based on the broad and general conclusions from UNDP´s Country Program Document. The COSED program would have merited from a more focused analysis and conclusions on how to work.
Thirdly, a reading of the narrative reports suggests that there is a lack of an overall strategic method in how impact shall be achieved. As mentioned, the focus seems to be on the achievement of activities. Why and how these activities are singled out is less clear. In addition, UNDPs internal evaluation on the country program carried out by Independent Evaluation Office in 2019 pointed out that the lack of baselines, key assumptions and a clear intervention logic makes it challenging to assess impact. Furthermore, the UNDP country evaluation report recommended that a triple nexus approach should be used in order to address the difficult humanitarian, developmental and conflict challenges in Burkina Faso. The midterm program evaluation from May 2024 that evaluated the period from August 2019 to December 2023 claim that UNDP had a strategy of delegating responsibility for implementation, in particular to NGOs. The final report that was sent to Sida on October 30, 2025 mentions that a key lesson was that partners were not sufficiently involved in the planning of activities. The report concludes that many times partners were not invited to take ownership in the broadest possible sense to solve the identified problem. As a consequence, partners, on multiple occasions, did not fully understand how to design the activity in relation to the goal and many activities were not completed.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
